question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank marked [A].
solution:
The correct answer is '**up**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct phrasal verb is **"eat up"**, which means to consume something completely or greedily.
 
• In the context of the passage, the birds were eating all the harvested grains, leaving none behind — hence, “eat up” is the most appropriate choice.
 
• Other options do not form appropriate or meaningful phrasal verbs with "eat" in this context: 
 
 
• **Eat away**: implies gradual erosion, not fast consumption of food.
 
• **Eat off**: means to eat from the surface of something (like a plate).
 
• **Eat on**: not a standard phrasal verb in this context.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Sentence: *The farmers in our village were fed up with the birds that used to eat **up**__ all their harvested grains.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Eat up**: To consume completely — most suitable in this food-related agricultural context.
 
• **Eat away**: To erode or corrode — more suited to gradual damage.
 
• **Eat off**: To consume food from a surface — incorrect here.
 
• **Eat on**: Not a recognized or meaningful phrasal verb here.
